bottom_line: In ASCOT-LLA, atorvastatin 10 mg versus placebo reduced the primary endpoint of non-fatal MI plus fatal CHD (hazard ratio 0.64 [95% CI 0.50–0.83]).
implications: These data support that, in this hypertensive population with baseline total cholesterol around 5.5 mmol/L, atorvastatin 10 mg was associated with fewer non-fatal MI plus fatal CHD events than placebo (hazard ratio 0.64 [95% CI 0.50–0.83]; 100 vs 154 events). The document also reports reductions in several secondary endpoints (eg, total coronary events 0.71 [0.59–0.86] and fatal/non-fatal stroke 0.73 [0.56–0.96]) while all-cause mortality was not significantly reduced (0.87 [0.71–1.06]). Because the lipid-lowering arm was stopped early after a median 3.3 years, the results reflect this shorter follow-up.

major_points.text: Multicentre randomised controlled trial of atorvastatin 10 mg vs matching placebo in hypertensive patients with total cholesterol ≤6.5 mmol/L.
major_points.quote:
10 305 with non-
  fasting total cholesterol concentrations 6·5 mmol/L or less
  were randomly assigned additional atorvastatin 10 mg or
  placebo.

major_points.text: Planned follow-up was about 5 years; the primary endpoint was non-fatal MI and fatal CHD; analysis was intention to treat.
major_points.quote:
We planned follow-up for an average of 5 years, the
  primary endpoint being non-fatal myocardial infarction and
  fatal CHD. Data were analysed by intention to treat.

major_points.text: The trial used a PROBE design and included a double-blind lipid-lowering comparison.
major_points.quote:
The study uses the Prospective Randomised Open Blinded
 Endpoints (PROBE) design.23 In addition, by way of
 a two-by-two factorial design, ASCOT has included a
 double-blind randomised comparison

major_points.text: Treatment was stopped early after a median follow-up of 3.3 years due to a highly significant reduction in the primary endpoint.
major_points.quote:
Treatment was stopped after a median follow-up of
  3·3 years.

major_points.text: Primary endpoint was reduced: 100 vs 154 events (HR 0.64 [95% CI 0.50–0.83]).
major_points.quote:
100 primary events had occurred in
                the atorvastatin group compared with 154 events in the
                placebo group (hazard ratio 0·64 [95% CI 0·50–0·83],
                p=0·0005).

major_points.text: Serious adverse events and liver-enzyme abnormalities did not differ; one non-fatal rhabdomyolysis case occurred with potential confounding.
major_points.quote:

  liver-enzyme abnormalities did not differ between patients

  of rhabdomyolysis was reported
